headline: Shorts bring 81% of views but ~zero subscribers; episodes convert. Production owns the biggest lever (shorts→episode funnel + packaging); recording owns the second (build episodes around what retains — live stakes, confessions, AI bits — not long explainers).

production.title: Never ship the 'Highlight -' prefix — hook first, provenance as suffix
production.evidence: All five published Highlights flopped: Stablecoins to Zero 8 views, US Govt AI Rugged Us 50, Perp of Fortune 23, AI cloned us 92, burn desk 5 — retention vs-typical in the bottom decile (0.03–0.12 through their first third). Retitles to 'Hook | Underpod Ep N Clip' are underway (Ep 2 + Ep 4 clips done); impressions/CTR data landing ~Jul 13 will give the clean before/after.
production.recommendation: Standardize clip titling: hook first, '| Underpod Ep N Clip' suffix, 'Clip from Episode N — full episode: [link]' as the description's first line. Finish retitling the remaining Highlight ('Perp of Fortune') and the scheduled Jul 14 clip.

production.title: Wire the shorts→episode funnel — it's currently disconnected
production.evidence: Traffic: SHORTS = 4,525 views (81% of channel) but only 238 watch-minutes (8%) and ~1 subscriber gained across all shorts. SUBSCRIBER + direct = 524 views but 1,636 watch-minutes. Episodes gained 2–3 subs each; shorts ~0. The related-video link is still unset for the Ep 5 batch.
production.recommendation: Set the related-video on every short, pin a comment with the episode link + timestamp of the full segment, and add end screens on episodes/clips. Make this a standard yt_upload.py-era publishing checklist step.

production.title: Pick shorts by personality, not topic importance
production.evidence: Winners are all human moments/one-liners: lottery ticket 1,273 views, Halo 3 roast 986, skipped-his-party 674, dog food 469, Pico's shrooms 395, Jamie Dimon 392, 'Coinbase sticker' 380. Losers are all abstract concepts: building a stock with ChatGPT 4, agentic investor 11, Claude won't help 10, retail gambling 24.
production.recommendation: In clipify selection, the test is 'is a host being a character / is there a quotable roast'. Every episode has 2–3 of these — clip those first, concepts last.

production.title: Cut shorts to 10–20 seconds so they loop
production.evidence: Sub-15s shorts average >100% viewed (Dimon 145%, Bitcoin Bankruptcy 130%, govt-deleted-AI 109%) — looping feeds the Shorts algorithm. The 25–60s cuts hold only 30–48%.
production.recommendation: Default clipify cuts to a single punchline in 10–20s, starting mid-laugh; use 25s+ only when the bit needs setup.

production.title: Tighten the episode edit toward 45–55 min using the retention curves
production.evidence: Episodes run 60–85 min but median avg view duration is 3–7 min (Ep1 6:53, Ep2 6:10, Ep3 2:59, Ep4 4:28). The curves literally mark the cuttable stretches: Ep 4's cliff at 22:00 (Freeze functions), Ep 2's collapse mid perps-explainer (36–46 min), Ep 1's crater inside stablecoins-to-zero (63 min).
production.recommendation: In the edit, cut or heavily trim the explainer stretches the curves flag, even when the conversation was good. Keep a segment long only if it would survive as a standalone clip.

production.title: Build cold opens from the episode's best 60–90 seconds and tease the end-of-show bit
production.evidence: End-of-show payoffs go mostly unseen live (Ep 1's lottery bit sits at the 95% mark with only 3–5% of viewers left) yet the lottery short is the channel's #1 video (1,273 views). Cold opens today don't stop the first-4-minute bleed (retention 11–19% by the 5% mark on every episode).
production.recommendation: In the edit: cold-open with the single best moment (the fill landing, the confession, the clone reveal), tease the finale ('stay for the lottery tickets'), and clip end-of-show bits as shorts within 24h of episode publish.

production.title: Cadence is working — protect it
production.evidence: 5 episodes in 4 weeks plus a daily short queue took the channel 0 → 16 subs and 6,169 views in 26 days; every episode day shows a views + watch-time spike.
production.recommendation: Keep weekly episode + daily short in the publishing schedule. Re-pull after Jul 13 to add impressions/CTR to packaging decisions (reach job created Jul 11).

recording.title: Don't spend the first 4 minutes on check-ins — 85% of viewers are gone by then
recording.evidence: By the 5% mark retention is 11–19% on every episode (Ep1 17%, Ep2 19%, Ep3 11%, Ep4 18%), and every episode records housekeeping/Pico updates in minutes 1–5 (Ep1 10:11, Ep2 5:42, Ep3 0:54, Ep4 2:13) before real content.
recording.recommendation: Record the welcome + check-in in under 60 seconds and get to the first real segment immediately. Save Pico/gamer-thumb updates as mid-show palate cleansers (the edit can only reorder what's recorded as discrete segments — keep them self-contained).

recording.title: Cap explainers at ~8 minutes and anchor them to live stakes
recording.evidence: Ep 4's biggest cliff (7%→4%) lands at 22:00, exactly where 'Freeze functions & privacy zones' starts inside a 24-min L2 deep-dive. Ep 2 collapses (vs-typical 0.22→0.07) mid 19-min perps explainer. Ep 1 craters to 3% inside the 13-min stablecoins-to-zero segment — the same content that got 8 views as a standalone clip.
recording.recommendation: When a topic needs explaining, do it in ≤8 min and tie it to something live or personal — explain perps WHILE the position is open (Eps 3/5 proved this retains). If it can't be tied to stakes, it's a candidate to skip.

recording.title: Make live stakes, confessions, and AI bits the spine — and put one in the first 10 minutes
recording.evidence: Ep 3's back half holds 0.64–0.95 vs-typical through the live-trade/custody/confession stretch; 'Confession: emergency fund into Stretch' sits at its 0.91–0.95 peak. Ep 4 peaks (0.73–0.86) at 'our jobs are fine, yours aren't' and recovers from its cliff when soul.md/AI-clone content starts. Ep 5 opened Perp of Fortune at 27:08 — after most viewers already left.
recording.recommendation: Structure every recording around one live-stakes bit (Perp of Fortune), one confession/personal-money story, and one AI-does-something-unsettling segment, with one of the three in the first 10 minutes.

recording.title: Manufacture clip-able moments on purpose
recording.evidence: The channel's reach is 81% shorts-driven, and every winning short is a host being a character or a quotable one-liner (lottery 1,273, Halo 3 986, skipped-party 674). These currently happen by accident.
recording.recommendation: Once per segment, someone states the take as a single quotable sentence ('Base is just Optimism with a Coinbase sticker' worked). Roast each other on the record — it's the best-performing content type.

experiments: [prod] Compare CTR/views on the retitled clips vs the five that shipped with 'Highlight -' once impressions data lands (~Jul 13).
[rec] Ep 6: open with Perp of Fortune in the first 10 minutes (continuity from Ep 5 is already planned) and compare the 5–25% retention band vs Eps 1–5.
[prod] Cut one 10–15s loop-style short from Ep 6 and A/B against a 30s+ setup short from the same segment.
[prod] Set related-video + pinned episode-link comments on the whole Ep 5 shorts batch, then watch whether SHORTS-source watch-minutes and subs move over 2 weeks.
[rec] Have each host bring one 'confession' story to Ep 6 — confessions sit at every episode's retention peak.
